getAbout.title: About
getAbout.name: Cristopher Cervantes
getAbout.headline: Engineering Manager & Tech Lead. AI products, serverless AWS and the teams that ship them.
getAbout.summary: Engineering Manager and Tech Lead with 9+ years shipping production software. At PSL Group I run engineering for four products, and shipped Claude agents on AWS Bedrock, a React codebase serving three brands and the pipelines every team deploys through. I lead through 1:1s and code reviews, and I still write plenty of the code.
getAbout.description:
I started like everyone else, as an intern who could barely scratch out a few lines of code. Over 9+ years I climbed one step at a time, until I became one of the key developers at every company I've worked for.

I challenge myself every day and I'm always after continuous improvement, both in myself and in the products I help build.

Today I'm a mix of Engineering Manager and Tech Lead. I don't just set the priorities for my products, I also suggest alternatives and solutions to the code my developers propose, and push them so that together we always land a better result.

Off the clock I love working out, spending time with my family, and every now and then reading some manga or playing video games. Some of them left relics on this page, and every one of them wants to be touched.

principles.title: Unblock first
principles.body: A blocked engineer costs more than any clever code I could write myself, so their questions jump my queue.

principles.title: Push back with an alternative
principles.body: A review that only says no teaches nothing. I bring another way to do it, and we pick the better one together.

principles.title: Boring and correct
principles.body: Especially with AI. A plain answer that's right beats a brilliant one that's wrong, every time.

principles.title: Readable at 2 AM
principles.body: Whoever gets paged tonight should understand the code without me in the room.

highlights: Where I learned the fundamentals I still lean on: algorithms, data structures, databases, networks and software engineering.
Part of TecNM, Mexico's national network of public engineering schools.

getProjects.title: PSL Group
getProjects.description: I run engineering for four of PSL Group's products: DGPL, AMI, IDH and MEC. I set the priorities, lead the team and still review and write plenty of the code.
getProjects.detailed_description:
I joined as Tech Lead on FirstWord, PSL's pharma and healthcare intelligence platform, and grew into managing engineering across the group's products.

On FirstWord I built one React codebase serving three brands, FirstWord Manager (the Next.js workspace the team runs everything from) and FirstWord AI, versioned Claude agents on Bedrock with streaming and guardrails.

Today I split my week between product and code: planning the roadmap for DGPL, AMI, IDH and MEC, running 1:1s, and pushing back on pull requests with alternatives until the team lands something better. I also own the shared deploy pipelines and the infrastructure as code, and set up the Claude Code tooling the whole team works with.
highlights: Grew from Tech Lead on FirstWord into Engineering Manager for DGPL, AMI, IDH and MEC
Shipped FirstWord AI: versioned Claude agents on AWS Bedrock with streaming answers and guardrails
Built a single React codebase that serves three FirstWord brands
Built FirstWord Manager, the Next.js workspace the team works from every day
Own the shared deploy pipelines and the infrastructure as code that every repo ships through
Set the roadmap, run 1:1s and code reviews, and rolled out Claude Code tooling for the whole team

getProjects.title: Grupo Tress
getProjects.description: Payroll and HR software used by companies across Mexico, the U.S. and Canada. I joined as a developer and grew into a Senior Developer leading features end to end.
getProjects.detailed_description:
As Senior Developer I led the self service app where employees track their own attendance, owning it from the first screens to production.

I also built GTI Controls, the React component library behind Interis Works, Tress's cloud payroll product, so every team shipped screens that looked and behaved the same.

Along the way I worked across the C# and Node.js services, the PostgreSQL databases and the cloud deployments on AWS and Azure.
highlights: Promoted from Developer to Senior Developer
Led the employee self service attendance app from the first screens to production
Built GTI Controls, the React component library behind Interis Works, so every team shipped consistent screens
Worked across C# and Node.js services, PostgreSQL databases and deployments on AWS and Azure

getProjects.title: Hisense México
getProjects.description: Internal tools for the corporate office and the factory floor, including the IT ticketing system.
getProjects.detailed_description:
I built the IT ticketing system from scratch in C#, ASP.NET MVC and SQL, and it became how the whole office asked for help.

I also worked on the corporate website and wrote tools that connected to internal systems so managers could follow manufacturing performance in real time.
highlights: Built the IT ticketing system from scratch, which became how the whole office asked for help
Connected internal systems so managers could follow manufacturing performance in real time

getProjects.title: Umbrella Seguros
getProjects.description: Rebuilt the school insurance workflows on their management platform.
getProjects.detailed_description:
I worked on Umbrella's insurance platform with C#, MVC, SQL, Python and JavaScript. I rebuilt the school insurance workflows from the ground up.

As more customers came on I kept extending the core features, fixing UX problems and tightening the business logic so the platform could grow with them.
highlights: Rebuilt the school insurance workflows from the ground up
Extended core features, fixed UX problems and tightened business rules as the customer base grew

getProjects.title: Systems Communications
getProjects.description: Internship. Built the truck log for the Tijuana customs office, my first code in daily use.
getProjects.detailed_description:
During my internship I built an inventory system for the Tijuana customs office that logged trucks coming in and out, written in PHP, C# and SQL.

It was the first time something I wrote got used every day by real people, and the reason I never looked back.
highlights: Built the inventory system that logged every truck in and out of the Tijuana customs office

getSkills.title: Leading Teams
getSkills.description: I mentor engineers, run 1:1s and code reviews, set priorities and keep releases on a steady schedule. I'd rather unblock five people than write the clever thing myself.
getSkills.effect: Once per sprint: every engineer on your side of the field is unblocked.

getSkills.title: AI & LLMs
getSkills.description: LLM features are still features: they need guardrails, tests and a fallback for when the model gets it wrong. I've shipped AI that people use every day, and I'd take a boring correct answer over a flashy wrong one.
getSkills.effect: When a model hallucinates, negate it and return a grounded answer instead.

getSkills.title: Cloud & Infra
getSkills.description: Functions when traffic is spiky, containers when it isn't. Every environment lives in code and every repo ships through the same pipeline, so deploys are boring in the best way.
getSkills.effect: Cannot be destroyed by a Friday deploy.

getSkills.title: Frontend & UX
getSkills.description: Design systems and component libraries a whole product, or several brands, can share. I sweat the small stuff too: loading states, dark mode, i18n and copy that sounds like a person wrote it.
getSkills.effect: Flip every loading spinner on the field into a skeleton.

getSkills.title: Data & Search
getSkills.description: I model data around how it gets read, then make sure the indexes agree. NoSQL when the access patterns are known, SQL when the data has real relationships, and a search engine when people need to find things fast.
getSkills.effect: Search your deck for any record and add it to your hand. Indexed, of course.

getSkills.title: Quality & Security
getSkills.description: Unit tests for the logic, end to end tests for the flows people actually click, and CI that blocks the merge when they fail. Logging, alerts and locked down secrets go in before launch, not after the first incident.
getSkills.effect: Negate any attack that skipped CI.

getCaseStudies.title: FirstWord AI
getCaseStudies.summary: Claude agents on AWS Bedrock that answer questions about pharma and healthcare intelligence.
getCaseStudies.challenge: FirstWord readers make decisions on what they read, so an AI feature there has to be right before it can be impressive. A confident wrong answer costs more than no answer at all.
approach: Versioned every agent, so a prompt or model change ships and rolls back like any other release
Streamed answers to the reader while the model is still writing
Put guardrails in front of every response
Treated the model like any other dependency: tested, monitored and with a fallback
getCaseStudies.outcome: AI answers that live inside the product people already use, held to the same bar as the rest of it.

getCaseStudies.title: One codebase, three brands
getCaseStudies.summary: A single React codebase that serves every FirstWord brand.
getCaseStudies.challenge: Three brands that each need their own look would normally mean three apps drifting apart.
approach: Built one React codebase with the brand as configuration, not as a fork
Shared components, data fetching and tests across every brand
Built FirstWord Manager in Next.js as the workspace the team runs everything from
getCaseStudies.outcome: A fix or a feature lands once and every brand gets it.

getCaseStudies.title: Pipelines every team ships through
getCaseStudies.summary: Shared deploy pipelines, infrastructure as code and Claude Code tooling for the whole team.
getCaseStudies.challenge: Every repo deploying its own way makes releases slow to review and scary to run.
approach: Moved environments into infrastructure as code
Built shared GitHub Actions workflows that every repo reuses
Set up the Claude Code tooling and conventions the team works with day to day
getCaseStudies.outcome: Deploys are boring in the best way, and a new repo is ready to ship on day one.

getCaseStudies.title: GTI Controls
getCaseStudies.summary: The React component library behind Interis Works, Tress's cloud payroll product.
getCaseStudies.challenge: Several teams building one payroll product were shipping screens that looked and behaved differently.
approach: Built a shared React component library for the whole product
Gave every team the same building blocks for forms, tables and layout
getCaseStudies.outcome: Every team shipped screens that looked and behaved the same.

getCaseStudies.title: Employee self service
getCaseStudies.summary: The app where employees track their own attendance, led from the first screens to production.
getCaseStudies.challenge: Employees needed to see and manage their own attendance without going through HR for every question.
approach: Owned the app end to end, from the first screens to production
Built on the C# and Node.js services and the PostgreSQL data behind Tress's payroll
getCaseStudies.outcome: Employees track their attendance themselves, in a product used by companies across Mexico, the U.S. and Canada.

getCaseStudies.title: IT ticketing system
getCaseStudies.summary: An IT help desk built from scratch for Hisense's corporate office.
getCaseStudies.challenge: The office had no single place to ask IT for help or follow up on a request.
approach: Built the ticketing system from scratch in C#, ASP.NET MVC and SQL
Kept it simple enough that nobody needed training to file a ticket
getCaseStudies.outcome: It became how the whole office asked for help.
